d: The HR Business Partner (HRBP) is a strategic and hands-on role responsible for aligning people strategy with business priorities, acting as the primary HR point of contact and trusted advisor to the leadership of an assigned business area within Independent Food Company. The role supports the company’s multi-brand operations, people-intensive service model and continued geographical expansion.

The role is accountable for delivering the full employee lifecycle within the assigned area, encompassing workforce planning, talent acquisition, onboarding, performance management, talent development, employee relations, engagement, reward and HR compliance, with a strong emphasis on productivity, retention, labour-cost discipline and a positive employee experience.

The HRBP may be aligned either to Head Office, partnering with corporate support functions, or to Brand & Operations, partnering with brand and operations leadership across a multi-site restaurant portfolio. The core accountabilities of the role are the same in both alignments; the specific focus areas for each are set out in Section 6 below.

While the position is a strategic business partner, the successful incumbent must be equally comfortable operating at a hands-on, operational level, particularly during new restaurant openings, organisational change, high-volume hiring periods and complex employee relations matters.
q: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration, Psychology or a related field. Relevant postgraduate qualifications preferred.
Recognised professional qualifications such as CIPD (Level 5 or above), SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP or equivalent are advantageous.

7–10 years of progressive HR experience, including at least 3–5 years in an HR Business Partner or senior HR generalist role, preferably within multi-site F&B, hospitality, retail or other high-volume service environments.

Strong working knowledge of the labour law and HR operations in the country where the role is based, including employee relations case management, visa and work permit processes, payroll requirements and HR compliance . .

Proven experience in workforce planning, specialist and high-volume recruitment, performance management and organisational change. Experience supporting new restaurant or site openings is highly desirable for the Brand & Operations alignment.
r: Act as a trusted advisor to the leadership of the assigned business area, translating business plans and priorities into a clear annual people plan aligned with Independent Food Company’s HR strategy.
Lead workforce and manpower planning in partnership with Finance and business leaders, ensuring headcount, organisational structures and labour costs remain within approved budgets.
Advise on organisation design, role clarity, reporting lines and spans of control to support business growth, new brand launches and changing operational requirements.
Analyse and interpret HR data, including turnover, absenteeism, overtime, labour cost and engagement trends, providing actionable insights and recommendations to leadership.
Lead and support organisational change initiatives, including restructures, transfers and integrations, through effective change management, stakeholder communication and employee consultation.

Partner with the Talent Acquisition team to plan and deliver recruitment for the assigned area, ensuring vacancies are filled with the right quality of talent within agreed timelines and approved budgets.
Ensure robust selection practices, including approved manpower requisitions, competency-based interviews, reference checks and offer governance in line with grading and approval frameworks.
Oversee structured onboarding and induction, ensuring timely completion of joining formalities, documentation, probation reviews and confirmation decisions.
Coordinate with HR Operations and Government Relations to ensure timely processing of visas, work permits, medical tests and other mandatory employment requirements.
Support the achievement of Nationalisation objectives for the assigned area through targeted sourcing, development and retention of national talent.
Drive the annual performance management cycle for the assigned area, including objective setting, mid-year and year-end reviews, calibration and timely completion of appraisals.
Coach line managers to set clear expectations, deliver constructive feedback and manage under-performance through structured performance improvement plans.
Identify training and development needs and partner with Learning & Development to deliver relevant technical, leadership, service and mandatory training programmes.
Lead talent reviews and succession planning for critical and leadership roles, identifying high-potential employees and building strong internal talent pipelines.
Promote internal mobility, career pathways and promotion from within, ensuring transparent, fair and merit-based career progression.

Act as the first point of escalation for employee relations matters, advising managers on grievances, disciplinary cases, investigations and terminations in line with company policy and applicable labour law.
Conduct or oversee fair, timely and well-documented investigations, ensuring consistent decision-making and minimising legal and reputational risk.
Lead employee engagement initiatives, including engagement survey follow-up and action planning, to strengthen morale, wellbeing and retention.
Analyse turnover and exit interview data, identifying the root causes of attrition and implementing targeted retention actions with business leaders.
Foster a culture of integrity, respect, inclusion and accountability across a diverse, multinational workforce, championing Independent Food Company’s values and employer brand.
HR Governance, Compliance, Reward & HR Operations
Ensure full compliance with Local Labour Law, related regulations and company HR policies, maintaining accurate, audit-ready employee records and documentation.
Partner with HR Operations and Payroll to ensure accurate HRIS data and timely, accurate payroll inputs, including attendance, leave, overtime and employee movements.
Support compensation and benefits processes, including salary benchmarking, job grading, annual increments, incentive schemes and offer approvals within approved frameworks.
Interpret and communicate HR policies and procedures to managers and employees, ensuring consistent application and recommending policy improvements where required.

Promote the adoption of HR systems, employee self-service and digital HR processes to improve efficiency, data accuracy and the employee experience, while maintaining strict confidentiality of employee information.
In addition to the core responsibilities above, the HRBP will focus on the following areas depending on the business area to which the role is aligned:
a) Head Office HRBP – Corporate Functions
Partner with the heads of corporate functions to build the organisational capability needed to support a growing multi-brand business.
Lead specialist, professional and managerial recruitment, ensuring a strong pipeline of corporate talent and a competitive employer value proposition.
Support job evaluation, grading and role design for professional and specialist positions, ensuring internal equity and market competitiveness.
Drive leadership development, career planning and succession for managerial and professional staff across Head Office.
Act as the HR partner for central projects and change initiatives, supporting new function set-ups, restructures and the roll-out of company-wide HR policies and programmes.
b) Brand & Operations HRBP – Restaurant Brands & Outlets
Partner with VP Operations and Restaurant Management across a multi-site portfolio, conducting regular restaurant visits to understand people issues on the ground and support front-line managers.

Lead HR readiness for new restaurant openings , refurbishments, transfers and closures, including manpower plans, high-volume recruitment, onboarding, training coordination and timely mobilisation of staff.
Work with Operations to manage outlet manpower levels, rostering standards, overtime and labour cost as a percentage of sales, ensuring staffing is aligned with business volumes.

Manage front-line employee relations and welfare, including site-level grievances, disciplinary matters, absconding cases, and staff accommodation and transport standards in partnership with Administration.
Strengthen retention of front-line talent through recognition, structured career pathways (for example, crew to supervisor to restaurant manager) and focused action on early-tenure attrition.
